object.description: The object type, which is always `batch`.

endpoint.description: The Portkey API endpoint used by the batch.

object.description: The object type, which is always `list`.

code.description: An error code identifying the error type.

message.description: A human-readable message providing more details about the error.

param.description: The name of the parameter that caused the error, if applicable.

line.description: The line number of the input file where the error occurred, if applicable.

input_file_id.description: The ID of the input file for the batch.

completion_window.description: The time frame within which the batch should be processed.

status.description: The current status of the batch.

output_file_id.description: The ID of the file containing the outputs of successfully executed requests.

error_file_id.description: The ID of the file containing the outputs of requests with errors.

created_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the batch was created.

in_progress_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the batch started processing.

expires_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the batch will expire.

finalizing_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the batch started finalizing.

completed_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the batch was completed.

failed_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the batch failed.

expired_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the batch expired.

cancelling_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the batch started cancelling.

cancelled_at.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) for when the batch was cancelled.

total.description: Total number of requests in the batch.

completed.description: Number of requests that have been completed successfully.

failed.description: Number of requests that have failed.

request_counts.description: The request counts for different statuses within the batch.

metadata.description: Set of 16 key-value pairs that can be attached to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Keys can be a maximum of 64 characters long and values can be a maxium of 512 characters long.

trace_id.description: Unique identifier for the request trace.

value.description: Feedback value, an integer between -10 and 10.

weight.description: Weight of the feedback, a float between 0 and 1. Default is 1.0.

message.description: Confirmation message indicating successful feedback submission.

feedback_ids.description: Ids of Feedbacks created returned in the same order as input

value.description: Feedback value, an integer between -10 and 10.

weight.description: Weight of the feedback, a float between 0 and 1. Default is 1.0.

_id.description: Unique identifier for the log entry

headers.description: Request headers (only present when debug logging is enabled)

body.description: Request body (only present when debug logging is enabled)

headers.description: Response headers (only present when debug logging is enabled or request failed)

body.description: Response body (only present when debug logging is enabled or request failed). May be redacted for certain embedding models.

lastUsedOptionJsonPath.description: JSON path to the last used option in the config

created_at.description: Timestamp when the log was created

metrics.description: Analytics metrics object containing detailed metrics about the request

id.description: Unique identifier for the log entry

created_at.description: Timestamp when the log was created

is_success.description: Whether the request was successful (status code 200-299)

is_proxy_call.description: Whether this was a proxy call

cache_status.description: Cache status (e.g., HIT, MISS, DISABLED, SEMANTIC HIT)

stream_mode.description: Whether streaming was enabled (1) or not (0)

parent_span_id.description: Parent span ID in distributed tracing

source.description: Source of the request (e.g., rubeus, proxy)

internal_trace_id.description: Internal trace ID for gateway tracking

last_used_option_index.description: Index of the last used option in the config

log_store_file_path_format.description: Path format version for log storage

request_parsing_time.description: Time taken to parse the request in milliseconds

pre_processing_time.description: Time taken for pre-processing in milliseconds

cache_processing_time.description: Time taken for cache processing in milliseconds

response_parsing_time.description: Time taken to parse the response in milliseconds

gateway_processing_time.description: Total gateway processing time in milliseconds

upstream_response_time.description: Upstream provider response time in milliseconds

finalUntransformedRequest.description: The original request before any transformations (only present when debug logging is enabled)

originalResponse.description: The original response from the provider (only present when debug logging is enabled or request failed)

transformedRequest.description: The request after transformations (only present when debug logging is enabled)

schema.description: Complete pricing configuration for a model

pay_as_you_go.description: Token-based pricing (all prices in USD cents)

request_token.description: Price object (value is in USD cents)

price.description:
Price in USD cents per token/unit.

Example: `0.003` = 0.003 cents/token = $0.03 per 1K tokens

additional_units.description:
Provider-specific additional pricing units.

Common additional units:
- `web_search`: Web search tool usage
- `file_search`: File search tool usage
- `thinking_token`: Chain-of-thought reasoning tokens (Google)
- `image_token`: Image generation tokens
- `video_duration_seconds_*`: Video generation (OpenAI Sora)

image.description: Image generation pricing by quality and size

value.description:
Reference to a value or rate.

Examples:
- `input_tokens`: Number of input tokens
- `output_tokens`: Number of output tokens
- `rates.request_token`: Request token rate
- `rates.response_token`: Response token rate

anyOf.description: Represents a streamed chunk of a chat completion response returned by model, based on the provided input.

id.description: A unique identifier for the chat completion. Each chunk has the same ID.

choices.description:
A list of chat completion choices. Can contain more than one elements if `n` is greater than 1. Can also be empty for the
last chunk if you set `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}`.

delta.description: A chat completion delta generated by streamed model responses.

content.description: The contents of the chunk message.

function_call.description: Deprecated and replaced by `tool_calls`. The name and arguments of a function that should be called, as generated by the model.

arguments.description: The arguments to call the function with, as generated by the model in JSON format. Note that the model does not always generate valid JSON, and may hallucinate parameters not defined by your function schema. Validate the arguments in your code before calling your function.

name.description: The name of the function to call.

id.description: The ID of the tool call.

type.description: The type of the tool. Currently, only `function` is supported.

name.description: The name of the function to call.

arguments.description: The arguments to call the function with, as generated by the model in JSON format. Note that the model does not always generate valid JSON, and may hallucinate parameters not defined by your function schema. Validate the arguments in your code before calling your function.

role.description: The role of the author of this message.

logprobs.description: Log probability information for the choice.

content.description: A list of message content tokens with log probability information.

logprob.description: The log probability of this token, if it is within the top 20 most likely tokens. Otherwise, the value `-9999.0` is used to signify that the token is very unlikely.

bytes.description: A list of integers representing the UTF-8 bytes representation of the token. Useful in instances where characters are represented by multiple tokens and their byte representations must be combined to generate the correct text representation. Can be `null` if there is no bytes representation for the token.

top_logprobs.description: List of the most likely tokens and their log probability, at this token position. In rare cases, there may be fewer than the number of requested `top_logprobs` returned.

finish_reason.description:
The reason the model stopped generating tokens. This will be `stop` if the model hit a natural stop point or a provided stop sequence,
`length` if the maximum number of tokens specified in the request was reached,
`content_filter` if content was omitted due to a flag from our content filters,
`tool_calls` if the model called a tool, or `function_call` (deprecated) if the model called a function.

index.description: The index of the choice in the list of choices.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when the chat completion was created. Each chunk has the same timestamp.

model.description: The model to generate the completion.

system_fingerprint.description:
This fingerprint represents the backend configuration that the model runs with.
Can be used in conjunction with the `seed` request parameter to understand when backend changes have been made that might impact determinism.

object.description: The object type, which is always `chat.completion.chunk`.

usage.description:
An optional field that will only be present when you set `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}` in your request.
When present, it contains a null value except for the last chunk which contains the token usage statistics for the entire request.

completion_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the generated completion.

prompt_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the prompt.

total_tokens.description: Total number of tokens used in the request (prompt + completion).

anyOf.description: Represents a completion response from the API. Note: both the streamed and non-streamed response objects share the same shape (unlike the chat endpoint).

id.description: A unique identifier for the completion.

choices.description: The list of completion choices the model generated for the input prompt.

finish_reason.description:
The reason the model stopped generating tokens. This will be `stop` if the model hit a natural stop point or a provided stop sequence,
`length` if the maximum number of tokens specified in the request was reached,
or `content_filter` if content was omitted due to a flag from our content filters.

created.description: The Unix timestamp (in seconds) of when the completion was created.

system_fingerprint.description:
This fingerprint represents the backend configuration that the model runs with.

Can be used in conjunction with the `seed` request parameter to understand when backend changes have been made that might impact determinism.

object.description: The object type, which is always "text_completion"

usage.description: Usage statistics for the completion request.

completion_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the generated completion.

prompt_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the prompt.

total_tokens.description: Total number of tokens used in the request (prompt + completion).

completion_tokens_details.description: Breakdown of tokens used in a completion.

reasoning_tokens.description: Tokens generated by the model for reasoning.

accepted_prediction_tokens.description: When using Predicted Outputs, the number of tokens in the prediction that appeared in the completion.

rejected_prediction_tokens.description: When using Predicted Outputs, the number of tokens in the prediction that did not appear in the completion.

prompt_tokens_details.description: Breakdown of tokens used in the prompt.

cached_tokens.description: Cached tokens present in the prompt.
